subject: Concordia cluster sizing: node slices & persistent disk affinity
messages:
From: Sam Truitt <sam.truitt@concordiahealth.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Mar 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Concordia initial: cluster sizing questions + affinity constraints

Jonas / Marissa,

Thanks for offering to review our requirements. Attached is a short spreadsheet (Concordia-Infra-Requirements.xlsx) with our anticipated pod classes and retention targets. A few of the high-level asks we wanted you to confirm: 

- Target RTO/RPO for model state (we expect ~30m RPO for inference KV cache recovery).
- Whether we should use node-affinity or pod-affinity for tenant isolation (we currently have strict rack pairing due to compliance).
- Guidance on PV classes: which workloads should be on encrypted SSD (NVMe) vs replicated blockstore.

We currently expect the cluster to start with 48 GPUs across 6 racks (8 GPUs/rack). Storage mix: 20 TB NVMe local per rack for hot KV, plus a networked replicated blockstore for longer-term model artifacts. We'll need your input on eviction and local PV fallback behavior.

Sam
Concordia Health — Infrastructure
Attachments: Concordia-Infra-Requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sam Truitt <sam.truitt@concordiahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Mar 2029 12:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Concordia initial: cluster sizing questions + affinity constraints

Sam —

Appreciate the spreadsheet. Quick read-through and initial recommendations below; we'll follow up with a short design doc and a proposal for a staged rollout. High-level answers first: 

1) RTO/RPO and KV cache: 30m RPO is achievable if we pair local NVMe with periodic async replication of checkpoints (every 10–15m). For KV cache we recommend: local NVMe for active working set + scheduled checkpoint to replicated object store so recovery stays under 20m under typical load.

2) Tenant isolation: Given your rack pairing constraint, prefer node-affinity + node-pool segmentation (rack-level node pools). PodAffinity is heavier and increases scheduling churn for large heterogeneous fleets. Node-pool segmentation also maps cleanly to Dedicated-style QoS boundaries.

3) PV classes: Propose three classes: 
   - hot-local-nvme (local, encrypted, NVMe) for KV and ephemeral cache; 
   - nearline-ssd (fast, replicated blockstore) for model artifacts with ~24–72h retention; 
   - archive-object (S3-compatible object store) for long-term artifacts/backups.

Eviction/fallback: define a PVPolicy CRD (we'll share a sample) that prefers local PV but falls back to nearline-ssd. If local PV eviction is required, the scheduler will attempt graceful checkpoint then move workload.

Next steps: Marissa / Irene and I will draft a 1-page cluster slice mapping (node pools -> rack groups -> PV classes) and a short runbook for failover. Can you confirm the expected per-GPU memory and typical sequence lengths for your inference workloads? That will drive NVMe sizing.

— Jonas
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-k8s-node-profiles.pdf (recommended profiles)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sam Truitt <sam.truitt@concordiahealth.com>
Cc: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Apr 2029 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Concordia initial: cluster sizing questions + affinity constraints

Looping in some specifics from infra requirements after running the numbers against our profile templates. Short technical notes: 

- Node pool sizing: For the 48 GPU start, recommend 6 node pools (one per rack) with uniform machine types: 8x A100-80GB equiv per node pool (split across 4 physical hosts/rack), so we avoid noisy neighbor issues on NVMe. Keep a separate 2-node control-plane tier in a non-GPU rack (small, encrypted disks).

- NVMe sizing: Assume KV working set per GPU ~120GB peak (based on sequence lengths + model KV growth). With 8 GPUs/rack that is ~1TB working set; we recommend 2x1.5TB NVMe per rack (for headroom and mirroring) but leave room for future expansion.

- PV policy and StorageClasses: implement storage classes with reclaim policies and allowedTopologies pinned to rack labels (topology.kubernetes.io/zone=rack-x). Example names: hot-local-nvme (volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer, allowedTopologies: rack label), nearline-ssd (ReadWriteOncePod or ReadWriteMany via replicated CSI), archive-object (external).

- Encryption & key management: all local NVMe should be LUKS-encrypted with CMK stored in a customer KMS/HSM. We will provide sample KMS integration and init containers for key injection at node bootstrap.

- Eviction & checkpoint flow: preStop hooks trigger an immediate checkpoint to nearline-ssd, then PV unmount; a small operator will enforce drain order to preserve SLA. We recommend a grace period of 120s for checkpoint flush.

I'll attach a short YAML snippet of the StorageClass templates in the follow-up doc. If Concordia has strict retention for audit logs, we should also table a separate object-store retention policy.

— Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is very helpful. A few clarifications and actions from our side: 

- Per-GPU memory: our current targets are 96–128GB per GPU (model median ~100GB). We can push to 160GB for large sequences if needed.
- We confirm CMK in our on-prem HSM; please send the KMS integration sample and the LUKS init container details.
- For the rollout, we'd like a two-phase approach: (1) pilot with 2 racks (16 GPUs) and standard node-pools + local NVMe mirroring, (2) full ramp to 6 racks after pilot validation.

Action items: 
1) Redwood: share the cluster-slice mapping doc + StorageClass YAMLs and the PVPolicy CRD.
2) Concordia: share current sequence length distribution and a small sample of trace logs (anonymized) so you can validate the KV working set estimate.

Happy to take a 45min sync next week to finalize the mutual action plan. Can you propose two slots?

Sam Truitt
